summary: Household: Oklahoma, 6 people (married couple plus 3 children under 18, youngest is 3), no one disabled or 65+, household earned income about $91,400/year, one adult has job-based health insurance, owns home with no mortgage, about $3,000/year other income, under $2,000 in savings. Recommended: (1) Child Tax Credit, refundable part: income is well under the phase-out, so the household should get the refundable portion for the three children. (2) CHIP / children's health coverage (SoonerCare): the children's income limit is around 210% of poverty for a family of six, which is close to $91,400, so the children may qualify. A caseworker should verify the exact figure, including the income disregard and whether job coverage affects eligibility. Not recommended: SNAP (net income after deductions is above the limit), WIC (income above 185% of poverty, even though a child is under 5), free/reduced school meals (income above 185% of poverty, but check whether the school district uses Community Eligibility, which provides free meals to all students), EITC (income above the limit for three children), TANF, SSI, Medicaid for the adults (Oklahoma does not expand Medicaid to working parents), and ACA premium tax credit (the job offers coverage). Pregnancy status was not confirmed but does not change these results.
